title: Paid requests
summary: A buyer of a cash on delivery order says "I already paid." You check the proof and decide.

sections.title: What is a paid request?
sections.intro: Most cash on delivery buyers pay the delivery person with cash. But sometimes a buyer pays early, for example by bKash, to make sure you send the order. They then tell you "I paid" and show a screenshot. That message is a paid request.

blocks.title: Key facts
items: It is only for cash on delivery orders.
The buyer can only send it after you accepted (confirmed) the order.
The buyer sends one request for each order. Only one, ever.
The request has three things: the transaction number, the way they paid, and a proof file (a screenshot or photo).
You can accept or reject it. An admin can also decide.
It saves you time. The buyer sends the proof themselves, so you do not need to ask in a message or phone call.
It keeps one clear record: the transaction number and the proof are saved with the order.
It protects you. Nothing is marked as paid until you or an admin check it. A buyer cannot mark their own order as paid.
It keeps your sales and system commission correct, because only a checked payment makes the order paid.

blocks.title: How a request comes to you
steps: A buyer orders and chooses cash on delivery.
You open the order and press Confirm.
The buyer sees a "Mark as paid" form on their order page. They fill in the transaction number and the way they paid, and add a proof file.
The request appears in "Paid requests" in your menu.
A small number on the menu item shows how many wait for you. The dashboard box "Mark as paid requests to check" and the bell show it too.

blocks.text: If a buyer never sends a request, nothing happens. They pay on delivery as usual, and you record the payment on the order yourself.

sections.title: How to decide on a request

blocks.title: Step by step
steps: Press "Paid requests" in the left menu. The "To check" tab shows the waiting ones.
Open a request. Read the amount, the way they paid and the transaction number.
Open the proof file. Look at the amount, the date and the number on the picture.
Check your own bKash, Nagad or bank app. Search for the same transaction number.
If the money is there, press "Accept: mark as paid". The order becomes Paid.
If the money is not there, or the proof is wrong, press "Reject". Write a short reason, for example "I cannot find this transaction ID". The buyer can read it.

items.means: Waiting for you. Do these first.
You or an admin accepted. The order is paid.

blocks.text: A rejection is final. The buyer cannot send another request for that order. Check carefully before you press Reject.

items: Accept: the payment is added to the order for you, with the proof. The order shows as Paid. It counts in your sales and in your system commission.
Reject: the order stays unpaid. The buyer pays on delivery as normal. They see your reason.
Either way, the request stays in the list as a record.

items.q: Why do I see no paid requests?
items.a: Buyers only send one after you confirm a cash on delivery order. If nobody paid early, there is nothing to check.

items.q: Can the buyer send a second request if I reject?
items.a: No. One request for each order, ever.

items.q: I forgot to check one. What now?
items.a: It waits in "To check". Nothing is lost. But the buyer is waiting, so answer soon.

items.q: What if I accepted by mistake?
items.a: Open the order and reverse the payment that was added. Only do this if it really was a mistake.
